superseded_runs.reason: Both GUI baselines compiled; 223 Qt tests passed, one expected lowercase instead of the existing uppercase hex format. Stopped remaining work and corrected only the test expectation before a new complete Linux matrix.

production_source_comparison.interpretation: 293 runtime/build paths match the successful Linux source archive and commit. The only build-input difference from the successful core/CLI commit is one GUI regression expected string, lowercase to uppercase. Application implementation and all core/CLI test and build inputs are identical. Eight existing local user extensions are retained separately.

limits: No real hardware setting or telemetry measurement was verified.
Queries are restricted to family 1Ah/model 08h, PCI 1022:153a/BDF 0. LN2 decodes only 0/1; the performance word is opaque and does not provide physical core mapping or power units.
Per-core/CCD PM layout and dual-rail hardware writes remain unresolved; original VF consumers and SoC helper failures do not establish those contracts.
AMD PStates writes, other AMD platforms and Curve Shaper, remaining Intel server/board controls, dynamic memory/EC and broader native PM transport remain incomplete.
EL7 means Oracle Linux 7.9 x86_64. Windows/macOS validate the portable core, not a complete application port.
QEMU verifies module integration only; actual register settings and Secure Boot were not tested.

visual_review.notes: Visually inspected six EL7 and Ubuntu 24.04 synthetic-backend fixtures. Query controls, explicit index, uppercase raw word, unknown LN2 value, no-setting status and physical-mapping limitation are visible without clipped results. No target hardware was used.

original_instruction_replay.scope: Complete original instructions. Synthetic PCI/MSR/EC, PM refresh/get_pm boundaries, labels and float vectors. No firmware execution, actual PM layout, voltage or physical mapping is established.

findings: Original VF MSR helper reads C0010293, uses FID[7:0], DID[13:8], VID[21:14], ignores read status and faults on zero DID. Its integer voltage expression is 245+5*VID; it is not the nine-bit dual-rail encoding.

stream_vftf uses existing Voltage/Temp/Freq Ghz/Eff Freq rows after synthetic refresh_monitor(0)/get_pm(4) boundaries. Zero frequency rows are omitted and outputs compacted. This is not an independent PM layout or physical mapping.
Original ln2_en calls EC::Rd_ECRAM(offset 4C, bank 2) and returns AL bit 3. Ghidra loses the member-call ABI; original instructions and 256 synthetic bytes confirm the arguments.

ForceSocVid writes its raw input to the selected response register, then sends FD/14; UnForceSocVid writes zero there and sends FD/FD/15. Both read and publish argument before response and continue through every injected PCI failure.
The independent Shimada settings define RSMU A6/5C queries; only A6 words 0/1 are decoded. The performance word is opaque; index bound 0..127 is application policy, not proof of topology or unit.
SetOverclockCpuVid takes an opaque single uint. It does not independently confirm dual-rail bit fields, physical targets, safe voltage limits or readback. Rails hardware writes remain unavailable.
limits: Seven REA function lengths are shorter than original ELF symbols; every difference is recorded and instruction replay uses full original symbol bytes.
No real hardware or original firmware executes in these experiments.
Synthetic labels, initial indices, MSR stack words, PCI responses and PM-return registers are explicitly chosen; they do not establish hardware validity.
PM per-core/CCD length/offset conflicts, dual-rail writes, dynamic EC controls and physical acceptance remain unresolved.

local_user_port_tests.environment: Windows without C++/Linux toolchains; compiler and Linux checks run in the cloud.
